subject.title: fix(security): bound hashFileContentsSync in approval script operand reads

question: Should approval-backed `system.run` impose an unconditional 8 MiB maximum on script operands, knowingly rejecting existing larger scripts rather than offering a separately approved policy path?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically narrow, but the selected hard limit establishes a user-visible security policy and compatibility boundary that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Adopt the 8 MiB hard limit
options.body: Accept fail-closed denial for scripts over 8 MiB and require end-to-end proof that the approval flow reports the denial cleanly.

options.title: Choose a different bounded policy
options.body: Set an explicitly reviewed limit or introduce an existing-policy-based path that preserves security without silently choosing 8 MiB as the permanent threshold.

recommendation.title: Adopt the 8 MiB hard limit
recommendation.body: Accept fail-closed denial for scripts over 8 MiB and require end-to-end proof that the approval flow reports the denial cleanly.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the clearest current-history owner of the mutable script-operand approval binding that the cap modifies.
